name: Log Shattering / Star Number (logarithmic)
details: For every finite binary class with positive star number, $\log_2|\operatorname{sh}(\mathcal H)|\geq\log_2\mathrm S(\mathcal H)$; more precisely it is at least $\log_2(\mathrm S(\mathcal H)+1)$.
proof: An $s$-star has a center and, for every star coordinate $x_i$, a leaf differing from the center only at $x_i$.  Thus every singleton $\{x_i\}$ is shattered.  Together with the empty set this gives at least $s+1$ shattered subsets, so $\log_2|\operatorname{sh}(\mathcal H)|\geq\log_2(s+1)$.  For $s>0$, this implies the stated logarithmic relationship.
witness_verification: For half-intervals, log shattering is $\log_2 n$, while the star number is $2$; thus no reverse affine-linear bound holds.
